steps.title: Prepare LB broth
steps.instruction: Combine per liter: 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 10 g NaCl, and distilled water up to 1 L; adjust pH to 7.0, autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare King’s B broth
steps.instruction: Combine per liter: 20 g proteose peptone, 10 mL glycerol, 1.5 g K₂HPO₄, 1.5 g MgSO₄·7H₂O, and distilled water up to 1 L; adjust pH to 7.0, autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min. After cooling, add filter‑sterilized glycine to a final concentration of 4.4 g L⁻¹. Dispense 10 mL into each sterile test tube under aseptic conditions.

steps.title: Make alkaline picrate solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.5 g picric acid and 12.5 g Na₂CO₃ in double‑distilled water up to 1 000 mL, mix until fully dissolved, store in a tightly closed amber bottle at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare ferrocyanide standards
steps.instruction: Using the conversion 422.4 g K₄[Fe(CN)₆] = 156 g CN⁻, prepare 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 ppm CN‑equivalent solutions by dissolving appropriate amounts of K₄[Fe(CN)₆] in 10 mL double‑distilled water per tube; cover immediately to avoid evaporation.

steps.title: Cut and sterilize filter paper
steps.instruction: Cut Whatman No. 1 filter paper into 12 × 1 cm strips, mark each strip at 10 cm with a pencil, autoclave the strips inside an autoclavable bag.

steps.title: Soak filter strips in picrate
steps.instruction: Immerse the sterilized strips in the alkaline picrate solution for 1–2 min, allow excess solution to drip off in a laminar‑flow hood, and use immediately or store in sterile sealed containers.

steps.title: Grow bacterial overnight culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate the purified bacterial strain into pre‑prepared LB broth, incubate overnight at 28 ± 2 °C with shaking at 150–180 rpm; prepare a blank tube under the same conditions.

steps.title: Inoculate test tubes with culture
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 % (v/v) of the overnight culture into each test tube containing 10 mL King’s B broth (with glycine) and incubate at 28 ± 2 °C until the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ ≈ 1.0 (idiophase).

steps.title: Hang filter strips in tubes
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, hang a picrate‑soaked filter strip vertically inside each test tube so that 10 cm of the strip remains in the headspace above the broth without touching the liquid.

steps.title: Seal and incubate tubes
steps.instruction: Seal each tube tightly with a Suba seal or rubber stopper, wrap the seal with Parafilm to ensure airtightness, and incubate at 28 ± 2 °C for 14 days without disturbance.

steps.title: Set up standard curve tubes
steps.instruction: Place a picrate‑soaked filter strip into each sterile test tube containing 10 mL of the prepared potassium ferrocyanide standard solutions (0–50 ppm CN⁻). Seal and incubate under the same conditions (28 ± 2 °C, 14 days).

steps.title: Elute color from standard strips
steps.instruction: After 14 days, cut each standard strip at the 10 cm mark with sterile scissors, place the cut strip into 10 mL double‑distilled water in a clean tube or beaker, and gently shake or vortex until the isopurpurate color is fully eluted.

steps.title: Elute color from bacterial strips
steps.instruction: Repeat the cutting and elution procedure for strips recovered from the bacterial culture tubes and the blank, using 10 mL double‑distilled water and identical shaking conditions for all samples.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 625 nm
steps.instruction: Using a spectrophotometer, record the absorbance (OD) of each eluted solution at 625 nm.

steps.title: Calculate HCN concentration
steps.instruction: Plot the OD values of the ferrocyanide standards against their known CN⁻ concentrations to generate a standard curve. Use the curve to determine the CN⁻ (and thus HCN) concentration of each bacterial sample. Apply the linear regression formula x = y/0.0013 − 0.0076, where x is HCN concentration (ppm) and y is the measured OD₆₂₅.

description: Validation of protocol 1. The absorbance values were compared with the standard curve of potassium ferrocyanide. The calculation of HCN concentration is based on the dissociation of potassium ferrocyanide. It dissociates into four K + ions and one [Fe (CN) 6 ] -4 ion, which further dissociates into six CN- ions in an aqueous condition [7]. Reaction equation: [ F e ( C N ) 6 ] K 4 · 3 H 2 O → [ F e ( C N ) 6 ] - 4 + 4 K + [ F e ( C N ) 6 ] - 4 ⇔ H + F e + 2 + 6 C N - → H + 6 H C N 2. It was observed that two-thirds of the cyanide ions were involved in the formation of isopurpurate, while one-third went into the formation of carbonate ions [8]. This can be represented by the equation: C 6 H 3 N 3 O 7 + 2 H C N + N a 2 C O 3 → C 8 H 2 O 6 N a N 5 + H 2 C O 3 + N a O H Therefore, taking OD without prior calculation of CN- ion from the standard compound would not show the real value of produced HCN. 3. The OD value obtained from the quantitative assay represents the amount of isopurpurate compound formed, which was directly related to the concentration of CN- ion calculated from potassium ferrocyanide, which represented the value of HCN produced ( Table 1 , Supplementary Table S1). The above-mentioned methodology is the next advancement in the old traditional method to quantify HCN production by bacterial isolates. This method includes the colorimetric test for the eluted color of the isopurpurate compound in double-distilled water.
